did_you_know.text: The word “צו” is a strong form of command. In rabbinic interpretation, it emphasizes acting promptly and continuing faithfully.
Here, the word “deshen” means the ashes left from the offering, although elsewhere it is connected with fatness, abundance, and fertility.
The phrase “morning by morning” describes a regular action repeated every morning, not just something done on one particular morning.
“His fistful” means the amount the priest gathers in his hand; it is not a fixed volume like a cup or a liter.
A tenth of an ephah is an ancient measure of volume, but scholars do not agree on its exact equivalent in modern liters.
The words “muravvet” and “tופיני” describe ways of preparing the grain offering, and Jewish commentators have tried to determine which cooking or baking methods they refer to.
The difference between earthenware and bronze also fits the properties of the materials: earthenware absorbs, so it is broken, while bronze can be scrubbed and washed.
When the blood of a sin offering was brought into the Tent of Meeting, its meat was not eaten but burned. This differs from sin offerings whose meat the priests ate.
